name: Flamed (thermal)
process: An intense flame passes over the wetted face; its minerals expand at different rates and the water flashes to steam, so the surface layer fractures and flakes away in small pieces, leaving a smoothly textured, very consistent surface.
processSources: Polycor Inc. (quarrier), 'How to add a flamed finish to granite surfaces', read 2026-09-26, https://www.polycor.com/resources/how-to-add-a-flamed-finish-to-granite-surfaces/

admits.text: Stones with minerals of different expansion, such as granite and bluestone.
admits.source: Polycor Inc. (quarrier), 'How to add a flamed finish to granite surfaces', read 2026-09-26, https://www.polycor.com/resources/how-to-add-a-flamed-finish-to-granite-surfaces/

reason.text: Limestone and marble cannot be flamed: their calcium carbonate responds uniformly to heat and does not flake.
reason.source: Polycor Inc. (quarrier), 'How to add a flamed finish to granite surfaces', read 2026-09-26, https://www.polycor.com/resources/how-to-add-a-flamed-finish-to-granite-surfaces/
Polycor Inc. (quarrier), 'How to add a flamed finish to granite surfaces', read 2026-09-26, https://www.polycor.com/resources/how-to-add-a-flamed-finish-to-granite-surfaces/

dissent.text: Another supplier writes that certain hard limestones and marbles can withstand the process, and that a gold limestone turns pinkish when flamed.
dissent.note: the records follow the quarrier's rule; a flamed calcite stone would need a specimen

quartzTransition.source: Anthony J.W., Bideaux R.A., Bladh K.W., Nichols M.C. (eds.) Handbook of Mineralogy, Mineralogical Society of America, 'Quartz' (Mineral Data Publishing, version 1.2, 2001), http://www.handbookofmineralogy.org/pdfs/quartz.pdf
quartzTransition.conditions: low quartz is stable below 573 degC; a granite's quartz passes it in the flame

museumUse.text: The design flames Suzhou granite in the modern era (Chenghuai); that substance is not in the stone group's records.

unverified.reason: No measured roughness of a flamed face was read.
